oneOf.description:
All in-scope tasks resolved from recorded claims and/or exhaustive
reachable history from `basis_revision`.

`HistoryPolicy::Never` skipped Git inference while legacy tasks were
present.

Traversal hit a shallow-clone graft boundary before resolving all
legacy tasks.

Traversal hit an explicit commit, byte, or duration budget before
resolving all legacy tasks.

Unparseable historical task shapes or missing/corrupt repository
objects prevented full observation.

HistoryPolicy.description:
How a completion-history query uses Git history for legacy `done` tasks
that lack a persisted `closed_at` (`ADR-0074`).

oneOf.description:
Consult Git history only when at least one in-scope `done` task
lacks `closed_at`; return best-effort results with explicit
completeness status if history is incomplete or unavailable.

Never consult Git history. Legacy `done` tasks without `closed_at`
remain `unknown`.

Require complete reachable history from `basis_revision` whenever
any in-scope `done` task lacks `closed_at`; refuse with a typed
error rather than returning a partial historical answer.

aplan_add.description: Create a task with an explicit id and phase, or mint the next id in this plan's own convention (including its configured ULID strategy) and derive the phase from its cut. It accepts live initial states, every creation-time relationship, revisit scheduling and version impact; terminal history uses the CLI's evidence-resolving manifest ledger. With `members`, both identity fields are required: create that milestone and move existing live work from its source cuts in one guarded batch. Refuses before writing what `check` would reject after, by running the rules on the plan this would produce; what it would only warn about is named in `notes` instead.

cut.description:
The cut to place it in: its milestone id (`M-v0.8`) or the label it
reports itself under (`v0.8`). A plan with `require_cut_membership`
rejects a task in no cut.

id.description:
Explicit id. An ordinary add may omit it to mint from the plan
convention; a non-empty members request requires it.

integrates.description:
Work-task increment ids integrated by this task (must also appear in
`blocked_by` and belong to the same cut).

members.description:
Existing live task ids moved from exactly one source cut each into the
new milestone this add creates. A non-empty list requires `id`, `phase`,
and a `tags` entry equal to `milestone`, forbids `cut`, and reserves
`blocked_by` for milestone predecessors.

paths.description:
Globs this task owns. Without them its future evidence cannot be bound to
it (`APLAN023`).

phase.description:
Reporting phase. An ordinary add may omit it to derive from the selected
cut or plan; a non-empty members request requires it.

revisit_at.description: RFC 3339 instant for an initially blocked task.

root.description:
Repository root containing `.aplan.yml`, or that repository's configured
plan directory. Omit to use the server's launch context.

status.description:
Initial live status. Terminal history uses the CLI evidence-resolving
manifest ledger.

title.description: What the task is, in a line.

traces.description:
Document sections this task answers to, as `path/to/doc.md#anchor`. An
anchor that does not resolve is refused (`APLAN008`).

version_impact_reason.description: Why the declared version impact applies.

aplan_claim.description: Record that you are working on a task, so other agents sharing this Git repository and all of its linked worktrees can see the same local ephemeral claim. It never edits the task or its durable `owner`. Two agents cannot both be told they hold one task: the common-directory record is a compare-and-swap. Taking a held task needs `from` naming the displaced holder. Labels are attribution, not authentication; the response includes time, origin, source and coordination scope.

as.description:
The name to record. Otherwise `APLAN_OWNER`, then per-user `me`, this
repository's `git config user.name`, then the operating system's user.
Never read from `.aplan.yml`.

from.description:
Who the task is being taken from. Required when somebody holds it, and
checked rather than taken on trust.

root.description:
Repository root containing `.aplan.yml`, or that repository's configured
plan directory. Omit to use the server's launch context.

aplan_claim.name: aplan_claim

held_by.description: Holder name now holding the claim.

aplan_close.description: Close a task with evidence, resolved at L2 before it is written: a cited commit must be reachable from HEAD and touch the task's `paths`, a cited file must exist, and a cited test must be one a configured runner lists. Refuses exactly what the CLI refuses; evidence is a citation to be resolved, never a score the caller asserts. This agent tool never runs a test; it never starts `test.run` or `test.batch`. Focused L3 closure is an explicit trusted CLI or interactive action. It never fetches a url, and whatever nothing here could check is named in `unchecked` rather than left looking like a pass. `aplan_verify` resolves the whole plan.

inputSchema.description:
Input for `aplan_close`. Deliberately accepts ONLY `id`, `evidence`, and
optional `root` so no caller can supply a self-assessment score.

evidence.description:
Evidence as `kind:ref`, e.g. `commit:d213c9a`, `test:mod::name`,
`file:path`, `url:https://...`. Required: a status is a claim, and this
server will not make it without proof to resolve.

root.description:
Repository root containing `.aplan.yml`, or that repository's configured
plan directory. Omit to use the server's launch context.

inputSchema.title: CloseInput

aplan_version.description: Version of aplan that performed the close.

closed_at.description: Canonical RFC 3339 UTC timestamp recorded at close.

aplan_dep.description: Add or remove one dependency edge: `after` is the task that must finish first. `blocked_by` is the only ordering the model has and it was writable only at creation, so re-sequencing meant editing files by hand. Refuses before writing what `check` would reject after: a cycle, an id that does not exist, a cancelled blocker, or a done task acquiring an unfinished one. A milestone's `blocked_by` is which tasks are in that cut rather than what it comes after, so editing that is refused here and belongs to `aplan mv`.

add.description: True to record the edge, false to remove it.

after.description: The task it comes after, which must finish first.

root.description:
Repository root containing `.aplan.yml`, or that repository's configured
plan directory. Omit to use the server's launch context.
